Our Real Hybrid and Regional Teams (Real HART) approach is designed to foster collaboration, learning, innovation, and meaningful relationships while providing flexibility where appropriate. Because our workforce spans multiple countries, regions, and client needs, work arrangements may vary by role and location. Some positions offer hybrid or remote flexibility, while others require regular in\-office presence. For example, certain teams and regions, including some of our UK operations, have office\-based requirements. Your recruiter will discuss the specific expectations for the role you're pursuing during the interview process and keep you informed throughout the hiring journey. For employees located within a one\-hour commute of a Real Chemistry office, we require in\-person attendance two days per week, either from a Real Chemistry office or when working onsite with clients. While these guidelines reflect our current workplace model, we understand that everyone’s circumstances are unique. If you require additional flexibility, we welcome an open conversation with your recruiter and our HR team to discuss your needs and determine what may be possible.



Real Chemistry is an Equal Opportunity employer. We continually strive to build and sustain an inclusive and equitable work environment where our employees feel empowered to leverage all they bring from their personal lived experience and professional expertise, to make our team the best in the industry. We encourage motivated and qualified applicants to apply without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, ethnic or national origin, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information, marital information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where Real Chemistry operates. title: Freelance Associate Creative Director, Art
description:
**Description**


GSW is a healthcare advertising agency that creates strategically sharp, human\-centered ideas for brands in health and wellness. We bring together creative, strategy, medical, and client expertise to develop work that helps complex science connect with the people who matter most. At GSW, we believe great ideas begin with curiosity, empathy, and a deep understanding of human behavior.

**Role Summary**
----------------


We are looking for a Freelance Associate Creative Director, Art to help lead the development of compelling healthcare campaigns and brand experiences. This role requires a strong conceptual thinker and visual storyteller who can translate complex medical and scientific information into clear, engaging creative. The ideal candidate brings a sharp design sensibility, a collaborative mindset, and the ability to guide work from idea through execution across multiple brands or assignments.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Lead the development of creative concepts and visual solutions across multiple healthcare brands and assignments.
* Translate complex scientific, medical, and brand information into engaging, strategically grounded creative.
* Partner closely with copy, strategy, account, medical, and experience teams to develop integrated campaign ideas and deliver high\-quality work.
* Provide day\-to\-day creative direction to designers and other team members, offering clear feedback and maintaining high standards of craft.
* Present ideas persuasively to internal teams and clients, helping build alignment and momentum around the work.
* Support broader brand vision and creative direction while identifying opportunities for innovation, organic growth, and stronger client partnership.
* Review work for accuracy, consistency, and alignment with regulatory, brand, and business requirements.
* Help manage workflow, scope assumptions, and team output to ensure creative excellence across deliverables.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* Strong conceptual thinking and the ability to develop unexpected, strategically sound visual ideas.
* Excellent design craft and proficiency in industry\-standard creative tools.
* A sharp eye for detail and a commitment to producing polished, accurate work in a highly regulated category.
* Confidence collaborating across disciplines and building strong partnerships with internal teams and clients.
* Ability to present and sell creative ideas in a clear, engaging, and persuasive way.
* Experience mentoring or directing other creatives and helping teams do their best work.
* Adaptability, curiosity, and comfort working in a fast\-paced environment with evolving priorities.
* Working knowledge of healthcare, pharmaceutical, or wellness marketing and the nuances of regulated communications.

**Preferred Experience**
------------------------

* 8–10 years of relevant experience in advertising, with strong healthcare, pharmaceutical, or wellness agency experience preferred.
* Experience developing campaigns for HCP and/or patient audiences.
* Understanding of medical terminology and the ability to work effectively with medical and regulatory partners.
* Background leading work across multiple brands, business lines, or complex assignments.
* Experience presenting to clients and contributing to high\-level creative and strategic discussions.
* Familiarity with emerging tools, platforms, and creative technologies, including AI\-enabled workflows, is a plus.


The anticipated hourly rate for this position is $90 but may vary based on various factors such as the candidate's qualifications, skills, competencies and proficiency for the role.


At GSW, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. If your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to apply anyway. At times, we will consider transferable skills from previous roles. We also encourage you to join our Talent Network to stay connected to additional career opportunities.


GSW is a full\-service healthcare communications agency that goes beyond advertising to create personalized brand experiences that involve, inspire, educate and activate people through ongoing brand journeys. As one of the world's ten most\-awarded healthcare advertising agencies, GSW is hell\-bent not to replace the same old with the same old. This is achieved through a provocative premise — if other brands communicated the way healthcare brands do, how many customers would they have? GSW turns against this premise through discovery of beneath\-the\-surface customer insights that we impact with stories, simplicity and authenticity.


Work Here Matters Everywhere \| How are you inspired to change lives?

*Syneos Health companies are affirmative action/equal opportunity employers (Minorities/Females/Veterans/Disabled)*


As a Syneos Health freelance, temporary, or contract employee, you may be eligible to participate in the Company 401k match and benefits such as paid time off or benefits through provisions in the Affordable Care Act or State\-specific requirements depending on the terms of your employment. Syneos Health complies with all applicable federal, state, and municipal paid sick time requirements for temporary/freelance/contract employees.

title: Creative Director
description:
**The Problem**
 Flock's creative group is expanding as the company raises its standard of visual storytelling and campaign execution across brand, film, and digital experiences. This momentum creates a need for unified creative leadership to turn complex technology and public safety outcomes into compelling, human\-centered narratives. You will own that direction, driving the creative concept, visual identity, and craft bar across design, film, and motion.
   

  

**What You'll Own**
* Direct integrated campaigns, product launch narratives, and flagship brand films from initial concept through final delivery.
* Define and maintain the visual, cinematic, and editorial standards across design, motion, and video production to build a recognizable creative signature.
* Lead and mentor multidisciplinary craft teams, guiding discipline leads in art direction, storytelling, and creative critique.
* Establish operational systems, including reference libraries, templates, and production guidelines, that elevate quality while improving delivery speed.
* Partner with brand strategy and production leadership to translate executive goals into clear creative briefs and execution plans.


**What This Role Is Not**
* This is not a hands\-off review role, you will actively shape concepts, guide edits, direct art execution, and refine details across all mediums.
* This isn't a high\-volume template production management job, your main focus is establishing concept quality and narrative depth.
* This is not an isolated brand strategy position, you will work directly alongside production and cross\-functional teams to ship live campaigns.


**What You Bring**
* Proven track record leading multidisciplinary creative teams across art direction, design, motion, and cinematic film production.
* Deep portfolio demonstrating high\-craft visual design alongside narrative documentary or high\-paced commercial storytelling.
* Advanced fluency in the complete production lifecycle, including typography, editing pace, color grading, sound design, and finishing standards.
* Experience setting practical brand guidelines, design systems, and creative review frameworks for internal teams and agency partners.
* Ability to direct campaigns that balance emotional human narrative with clear technical product messaging.


**Compensation**
 In this role, you'll receive a starting salary between $200,000 and $250,000 as well as Flock Stock Options. Base salary is determined by job\-related experience, education/training, as well as market indicators. Your recruiter will discuss this in depth with you during our first chat.
   

  

 Why Flock 💚
   

  

 Every community deserves to be safe. Flock builds the technology that makes that real: last year we supported over 1 million criminal investigations and helped locate more than 10,000 missing people. We're 1,700 people building the impossible with over $1B in funding, and the expectations are high on purpose. If you want a role where the stakes are real and the pace matches, this is it.
   

  

 📍Some problems get solved faster in the same room, so we prioritize candidates in Atlanta and Boston. Hub\-based roles mean real in\-person time with your coworkers. Remote roles exist, and when a posting is open to remote work, it says so.
   

  

 🌟 The impossible takes every kind of mind. Flock is an equal opportunity employer, and we know the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, experiences, and skills working together with mutual respect. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, email recruiting@flocksafety.com; your information stays confidential and is used only to arrange the right accommodation for your interviews.
   

  

 💰 On compensation. We pay fairly for the work. Base salary is determined by job\-related experience, education, training, and market indicators. The range in this posting covers base salary only and doesn't include equity, sales bonus plans where applicable, or benefits. The range may be adjusted over time, and this posting may span more than one career level.
   

  

 📣 One last thing. All legitimate communication from Flock comes from an email ending in @flocksafety.com or noreply@ashbyhq.com. We never make offers through messaging apps or third parties, and we never request payment or sensitive personal information during hiring. title: Creative Director
description:
**About Us**
 Circle is building the world’s leading AI\-powered, all\-in\-one platform for digital businesses. We make it possible for creators, coaches, educators, and businesses to bring together their audience with engaging discussions, live streams, events, chat, courses, and payments — all in one place, all under their own brand.
   

  

 We’re proud to be a fully remote company of around 270 (and growing!) team members from 30\+ countries around the world. We seek exceptional individuals around the world, set them up to do the best work of their lives, and in turn, create a meaningful impact in their own lives. We don't track hours, but we do manage for high expectations very closely. We collaborate across time zones, are highly async, and like to document a lot.
   

  

 Twice a year, we bring the whole company together in beautiful places around the world for our company offsites. So far, we’ve hosted offsites in Turkey, Portugal, Mexico, Thailand, Colombia, Italy, Ireland, and more, with still more to come!
   

  

 Check out our
 **Careers** 
 page for more about working at Circle.
   

  

**About The Role**
**We’re excited to bring on Circle’s first Creative Director.**
 This is a unique opportunity to shape how Circle shows up in the world, and define the story of a generational company building the future of digital businesses.
   

  

 We’re looking for an exceptional creative storyteller who can help us develop strong, consistent narratives across everything Circle puts into the world: product launches, campaigns, ads, landing pages, announcements, partnerships, events, and more.
   

  

 You obsess over the power of a great narrative. You believe every word, visual, and detail matters. You have an exceptionally high creative bar, thrive in highly collaborative environments, and know how to influence people through the quality of the work itself.
   

  

 As Circle’s first Creative Director, you’ll first and foremost act as a creative extension of the founders. You will turn their ideas, product strategy, and company vision into narratives that are clear, memorable, and unmistakably Circle across all our assets.
   

  

 On a day\-to\-day basis, you’ll work closely with Circle’s founders and across our in\-house design studio, product marketing, paid media, video, and events teams to elevate our storytelling and creative execution across every major moment.
   

  

**Your goal is to help make Circle one of the most creatively distinct and definitive companies in the category of digital businesses.**
**What You'll Be Doing**
* Shape Circle’s narrative. Work closely with Circle’s founders to synthesize, sharpen, and evolve the story behind our long\-term vision, and translate it into clear, compelling narratives that can travel across everything we do.
* Own the creative direction of our biggest launches and campaigns. Find the angle, develop the brief, shape the story, and obsess over how we make each moment stand out. You’ll partner closely with Product Marketing across launches, announcements, demos, and enablement to ensure everything feels cohesive, intentional, and unmistakably Circle. Doing this well requires developing a deep understanding of our product, customers, and market.
* Be a deeply embedded creative marketing partner to our design studio. You’ll work especially closely with our Design Studio, which is led by one of Circle’s co\-founders and won’t report to you. Success here involves shared taste, mutual trust, healthy creative tension, and the ability to move quickly together. You’ll occasionally lead external agencies as well — and when the moment calls for it, write the high\-stakes copy yourself: the headline, manifesto, launch script, or line someone delivers on stage.
* Raise the bar on our advertising and creative campaigns. Develop the concepts and narratives behind Circle’s ad creative, partnering up our Paid Acquisition team to turn them into high\-performing campaigns. They’ll bring the channel and media\-buying expertise; while you can make sure the creative is worth paying to distribute.
* Direct how our stories come to life across video and events. Get hands\-on with scripts, structure, pacing, and narrative for launch films, social, ads, virtual summits, and other major moments. You won’t be editing videos or producing events yourself, but you’ll understand the craft well enough to have strong opinions about what works in each medium, and collaborate deeply with the specialists who bring it to life.
* Influence the narrative behind brand experiences people remember across our webinars, virtual summits, conferences, and live events to align with company brand vision. This includes everything from the theme and programming to the booth, talks, slides, copy, and small details nobody else would think to obsess over.
* Turn partnerships into stories. Work with our Partnerships team to make more of our collaborations with creators and customers into stories we can distribute across our channels. You can help develop the concept, framing, name, narrative, and creative execution behind our biggest partnerships, and helping our partners tell those stories powerfully themselves.


**What We're Looking For**
* A body of work you’re genuinely proud of. We care far more about what you’ve made than the titles you’ve held or the number of years you’ve been doing it. You should be able to walk us through your best work piece by piece: the problem, the idea, the choices you made, what you personally contributed, and ultimately, whether it worked.
* Exceptional creative taste and judgment. You know great work when you see it, can articulate why it’s great, and have the conviction to push work until it gets there. Just as importantly, you know when an idea is trying too hard, when something is off\-brand, and when your own fingerprints are making the work worse rather than better.
* You’re an exceptional storyteller and writer. You can take something complicated and find the simple, compelling story inside it. You care deeply about language and will happily obsess over a headline, a launch narrative, or a single line of copy until it feels inevitable.
* A strong point of view, and the ability to make it better through collaboration. We don’t want someone who waits for a brief and executes it. We want someone who can tell us what the brief should be, challenge the premise when necessary, elevate ideas coming from the team and our founders, and make a compelling case for a different direction.
* Real fluency in video as a creative medium. You don’t need to shoot, edit, animate, or produce. But you should deeply understand what makes video work, from the script and opening seconds to structure, pacing, emotion, and payoff. You should also understand why a great launch film, social video, customer story, and paid ad require very different creative choices.
* Experience making creative that has to perform. You’ve developed ads and campaigns where the work was ultimately accountable to results. You’ve seen the numbers, learned from them, iterated because of them, and know how to partner with paid acquisition teams without allowing performance marketing to turn into boring marketing.
* An instinct for getting attention without going off script. You understand how to make a brand noticeable, surprising, and culturally relevant without chasing attention for its own sake. Ideally, you can show us a creative risk you fought for that worked, and another you talked the room out of because it wasn’t right for the brand.
* The ability to lead through influence, not hierarchy. There’s no large creative organization reporting to you. Much of your impact will come from getting exceptional work out of designers, marketers, writers, video producers, agencies, and founders who don’t report to you. You know how to raise the creative bar without becoming a bottleneck.
* A great eye for design and deep respect for the craft. You don’t need to be a designer, but you should be able to work shoulder\-to\-shoulder with exceptional ones. Our Design Studio is led by a co\-founder and operates with a very high bar; you’ll need the visual taste, vocabulary, and collaborative instincts to be a trusted creative partner to that team.
* Experience working closely with founders. You’re comfortable working with founders who care deeply about the product, brand, and details. You will need to extract the vision, challenge it when needed, and turn it into something better than either of you would have arrived at independently.
* An obsession with understanding what how to tell the world about we do and why it matters. The best creative work here will come from understanding Circle at a deep level: our product, customers, competitors, category, and where the market is going. You should genuinely enjoy developing that level of context rather than treating it as somebody else’s job.
* Exceptional communication skills. Circle is global, remote, and highly asynchronous. You’ll need outstanding written and verbal English (CEFR C2 or equivalent), and the ability to make your thinking clear enough that great work can move forward even when everyone isn’t in the same room.


**Compensation \& Benefits**
 Circle offers U.S.\-benchmarked compensation globally, equity in the company with ongoing refresh grants, and 35 days of paid time off each year.
   

  

 We’re a remote\-only team that comes together twice a year for company retreats in incredible destinations around the world. Alongside incredible flexibility and autonomy, we offer a benefits package that supports health, wellbeing, and professional growth. Learn more in our Candidate Hub.
   

  

****Learn more****
* Candidate Safety \& Interview Process Notice
* Diversity, Equity \& Inclusion
* How We Use Candidate Data
* Equal Employment Opportunity
* Visit our Candidate Hub to learn more about working at Circle, our benefits, and our hiring process.


 Compensation Range: $171K

title: Design Director
description:
**About The Role**
 We’re hiring a Design Director to lead Product Design across our Spending, Savings, and Investing experiences. You’ll shape how millions of members interact with their money every day—from the experiences they rely on most often to the ones that help them build toward what’s next.
   

  

 This role calls for a leader who pairs exceptional visual craft with strong product thinking. title: HR Director

title: Senior Director, AI Transformation & Operations
description:
The Senior Director of AI Transformation \& Operations serves as the operational heart of the ELEC AI Center of Excellence.

You will provide the structure, shared foundations, and governance that enable our four business lines to deliver AI solutions with speed, quality, and precision.
**Job Description**
===================


**The mission of the AI Operations Leader within our office is to:**


* **Enable Execution:** Facilitate the execution of Business Line long\-term strategy (LTS) plans, ensuring they move at speed and with high impact.
* **Ensure Operational Excellence:** Define and manage the day\-to\-day mechanisms that deliver consistent quality, ensuring that every AI initiative is executed with discipline and minimal risk.
* **Scale Through Capability:** Act as the operational backbone of our center of excellence, transforming our strategy into repeatable processes that allow our businesses to own and scale their AI delivery effectively.

**What you’ll be doing**


* **Facilitating business execution:** You will act as the primary partner for our four business lines. Your focus is on clearing the path for them to execute their long\-term strategic AI plans, ensuring they have the support and resources needed to reach their goals quickly and effectively.
* **Defining the operational heartbeat:** You will establish the "cadence" of AI delivery—regular reviews, progress tracking, and feedback loops—that keep our business lines aligned and moving forward.
* **Providing a shared foundation:** You will lead the development of the "common ground"—the standards, tools, and shared platforms—that allow our business units to build AI solutions without having to solve the same infrastructure or governance problems in isolation.
* **Driving speed and quality:** You will help our business teams balance the need for rapid delivery with the need for high\-quality, reliable output. By implementing clear, lightweight ways of working, you will help teams avoid common pitfalls and keep projects on track.
* **Managing risk by design:** Instead of treating risk as a hurdle to be jumped at the end, you will help teams bake it into their processes from day one. You will ensure that Responsible AI and security practices are built into the workflow, protecting the business while maintaining momentum.
* **Ensuring strategic alignment:** You will oversee our portfolio to ensure that the work happening across the business lines stays tethered to ELEC’s overarching enterprise priorities. You will help teams focus their energy on the initiatives that provide the greatest return.
* **Supporting the transition:** We are working toward a future where our business lines are fully empowered to lead their own AI delivery. You will guide this evolution, scaling our efforts today to build a sustainable, business\-led model for 2030\.
* **Driving adoption and upskilling:** You will champion the human side of our transformation by leading efforts to upskill our workforce. In close coordination with ELEC HR, the GE Vernova Corporate Learning team, the ELEC CTO office, and Business Line AI teams, you will design and adapt training programs that directly address the unique missions and practical needs of our ELEC teams. By building targeted AI literacy and specialized expertise, you will ensure our people are empowered to adopt new tools and maximize the value of AI in their specific daily work.

**What you bring to the team**


* **A commitment to partnership:** You have a track record of supporting business units in achieving their strategic goals. You view your role as a service to the business lines, not as a central authority.
* **A "get it done" mindset:** You understand that the best strategy is only valuable if it can be executed. You are experienced in guiding complex initiatives through to delivery while maintaining high standards.
* **Balanced judgment:** You know how to provide enough guidance to ensure consistency across the company without creating unnecessary red tape that slows teams down.
* **Technical and business fluency:** You can communicate clearly with both technical delivery teams and business leadership, ensuring that everyone understands the goals and the path to achieving them.
* **Proven reliability:** You have a history of managing programs or operations where speed, quality, and risk management were all critical to success.

**How we’ll measure success**


* **LTS Execution:** Our business lines are successfully hitting the milestones set out in their long\-term AI strategy plans.
* **Operational Speed:** We have reduced the time it takes to get from an idea to a working, value\-driving solution.
* **Risk \& Quality:** Our AI initiatives consistently meet our internal standards for security and responsibility, with minimal friction.
* **Business Impact:** Every AI project we support can clearly demonstrate its contribution to ELEC’s business performance.

**Skills \& Academic Requirements**


To lead this transformation effectively, you will need a blend of technical understanding, operational discipline, and the ability to influence people.


* **Academic \& Professional Background:**
	+ **Degree:** Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
	+ **Experience:** Strong and proven leadership experience in operations, program management, or technical strategy, ideally within a large, global matrixed organization.
	+ **AI/Technical Fluency:** A solid grasp of the AI/ML landscape—not necessarily as a developer, but as a leader who understands the lifecycle of AI solutions, from data preparation to production and monitoring.
* **Core Competencies:**
	+ **Strategic Change Management:** Proven success in leading large\-scale organizational shifts, including the ability to build and sustain engagement across diverse teams.
	+ **Operational Discipline:** Exceptional ability to build, manage, and refine the "cadence" of a business—tracking metrics, managing budgets, and maintaining project momentum.
	+ **Cross\-Functional Collaboration:** Demonstrated expertise in bridging the gap between technical teams (CTO/Engineering) and business stakeholders. You know how to translate technical requirements into business value and vice\-versa.
	+ **Learning \& Development Agility:** A strong track record of partnering with HR and Learning \& Development functions to design curriculum or enablement programs. You understand that "upskilling" is not just about classroom training, but about driving behavioral change.
	+ **Influencing \& Negotiation:** The ability to achieve alignment across different business lines without having direct line authority over every team member. You lead through persuasion, shared goals, and the value you provide.
	+ **Risk \& Governance Mindset:** A pragmatic approach to compliance and ethics. You can integrate guardrails into the development process so that they feel like an asset rather than an obstacle.

title: Course Content Manager
description:
**Application deadline: 24 September 2026 at 17:00 (Barcelona time)**  

  

**Who are we?**  

  

EIT Urban Mobility is an initiative of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), a body of the European Union and Europe's largest network for transport innovation in cities.

  

Our mission is to accelerate change towards a sustainable model of urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. We connect public and private actors and provide them with access to markets, talent, finance and knowledge.

  

Using cities as living labs, our industry, research and university partners will demonstrate how new technologies can work to solve real problems in real cities by transporting people, goods and waste in smarter ways.

 **About EIT Urban Mobility Academy:**

  

Our EIT Urban Mobility Academy is a collaborative arena for lifelong learning, helping to build critical capabilities for innovation and transformation. We are training the next generation of urban mobility practitioners, needed by the urban mobility ecosystem of the future. The webpage of EIT Urban Mobility Academy is:  

https://www.eiturbanmobility.eu/academy/

  

Within the Academy, Urban Mobility Explained (UMX) offers a variety of training programmes and experiences on hot topics in urban mobility and transport for professionals and organisations around Europe. In close collaboration with universities, business schools, consultancies and mobility experts, this lifelong learning initiative uses different formats including light online material in a YouTube channel, online courses (asynchronous), and face\-to\-face (F2F) courses (on\-site, online synchronous and blended). More information on UMX: https://urbanmobilityexplained.eu/

 **Be part of a team where:**  

  

The **Course Content Manager** will play a pivotal role in shaping the present and future of UMX. Reporting to the Head of Professional Education, you will support the UMX team in maintaining operational excellence, ensuring full compliance, and successfully delivering UMX courses in compliance with EIT Urban Mobility and EIT requirements.

  

You will help shape the future development of the UMX portfolio by identifying emerging topics, sourcing expertise, converting knowledge into high\-impact learning experiences, and ensuring our content remains aligned with the evolving needs of cities, public authorities, mobility operators and industry stakeholders across Europe.

  

You will support EIT Urban Mobility's long\-term strategy by developing high\-impact courses that generate independent value and revenue within our five Priority Domains: (1\) shared and public transport (2\) urban logistics, (3\) mobility AI and data management, (4\) electrification and alternative fuels, and (5\) health and mobility.

  

As part of this role, you will support the development of EIT Urban Mobility's Autonomous Mobility Academy initiative. Working alongside internal and external subject\-matter experts, you will contribute to programme design, ecosystem building, expert sourcing, content governance, funding opportunities and project development activities.  

  

**Key responsibilities:**

* Knowledge Intelligence \& Cross\-Functional Collaboration: Monitor developments across the mobility ecosystem and identify reports, studies, project outputs and market insights that can be transformed into learning assets and new course opportunities. Collaborate with marketing, business development, learning and other EIT Urban Mobility teams, while contributing to wider organisational initiatives, events and thought leadership activities.

  

  

**What you will bring along the way:**  

  

**Must\-haves**

  

* 7\+ years of professional experience in urban mobility, transport innovation, mobility technology, innovation ecosystems or closely related sectors, including experience working with experts, knowledge products, training programmes or thought leadership initiatives.
* 3\+ years working experience(s) in managing/producing education or learning activities and trainings, preferably in a blended format (partly online, partly on\-site), ideally for a professional or lifelong learning audience.

**Who we are**
--------------


Glovo is part of the Delivery Hero Group, the world’s pioneering local delivery platform, our mission is to deliver an amazing experience—fast, easy, and to your door. We operate in around 65 countries worldwide. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Delivery Hero has been listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange since 2017 and is part of the MDAX stock market index.


### **Job Description**


We are on the lookout for a **Staff Product Designer** to join the **Order Tracking team** on our journey to always deliver amazing experiences.


Imagine shaping how millions of users track their orders across 70\+ countries, ensuring a seamless and delightful delivery experience.  

This role is key to ensuring our customers enjoy a delightful order tracking experience across multiple brands, including Talabat, foodpanda, PedidosYa, Glovo, HungerStation, and the rest of the Delivery Hero group of consumer apps.  

You will own and shape the order tracking product, ensuring millions of customers worldwide have a seamless delivery experience.


In our Logistics Team, you’ll tackle high\-impact challenges that make last\-mile delivery efficient, affordable, and sustainable. Your work will directly improve experiences for riders, end customers, and merchants across the globe. Each enhancement you contribute will help Delivery Hero optimize delivery operations, supporting expansion into new areas like grocery and retail.


Our mission in the Customer Product Line design chapter in Logistics is to balance internal users and customers needs, business goals and feasibility in order to build the best\-in\-class solutions that drive positive business outcomes.


We have 3 principles as a design chapter here:


Don't make me think! \- We design the best\-in\-class and high\-impact solutions with usability at its core, considering consistency across the products. We aim to bring trust and efficiency to our internal users in their daily tasks without compromising on the look and feel.


We help the biz to grow sustainably \- We know about the business/product line strategy and OKRs like the back of our hand. That's why, whenever we propose or start a new design initiative, we consider the positive impact that it may cause on the business.


Our customers and users matter \- We are responsible for bringing our users/customers and stakeholders' voices/needs to the table. We do it by research. We care about their satisfaction and consider it in our process.

* Shape the future of order tracking – This is your opportunity to lead the design efforts in revamping the order tracking experience across Delivery Hero’s brands.
* Drive impactful designs – You will own the end\-to\-end design process, from ideation to launch, ensuring intuitive, visually compelling, and efficient user experiences. Your designs will enhance usability while aligning with business goals and technical feasibility.
* Leverage data and insights – You will use data\-driven decision\-making, incorporating research insights, user feedback, and A/B testing results to refine and optimize the order tracking journey.
* Define and execute strategy – You will contribute to and refine the product roadmap, prioritizing features that drive engagement and improve the overall user experience. Your expertise in design systems will ensure consistency and scalability across platforms.
* Collaborate and Innovate – researchers, product managers, and engineers, you will co\-create seamless experiences that meet both user and business needs. You will facilitate workshops and design sprints to align teams and drive innovation.
* Advocate for design excellence – You will champion best practices in visual design, accessibility, and interaction design, ensuring that every touchpoint is thoughtfully crafted. Your ability to communicate design decisions effectively will help align stakeholders across the organization.
* Be a Leader and mentor – You will help foster a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration, and user\-centricity within the team, inspiring others with your design expertise and strategic thinking.

  


### **Qualifications**


The ideal candidate excels in user\-centric design for complex platforms, with strong visual skills and expertise in Figma and design systems. They are strategic thinkers, skilled in workshop facilitation, design metrics, and stakeholder management. A collaborative team player, they communicate effectively and drive alignment. Experience in B2C and animation is a plus.

* Experience and expertise: 5\+ years as a product designer, skilled in designing complex platforms (app experience essential) and contributing to design systems.
* Design and strategy: Strong visual design skills, user\-centric mindset, and strategic thinking, including workshop facilitation and design metrics analysis.
* Tools and communication: Proficient in Figma and prototyping tools, with excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
* Collaboration and bonus Skills: Team player who motivates others; experience in B2C products or animation concepts is a plus.


### **Additional Information**


* An enticing equity plan that lets you own a piece of the action.
* Top\-notch private health insurance to keep you at your peak.
* Monthly Glovo credit to satisfy your cravings!
* Discounts on transportation, food, and even kindergarten expenses.
* Discounted gym memberships to keep you energised.
* Extra time off, the freedom to work from home two days a week, and the opportunity to work from anywhere for up to three weeks a year!
* Enhanced parental leave, and office\-based nursery.
* Online therapy and wellbeing benefits to ensure your mental well\-being.

What you achieve matters and how you achieve it defines us. Together, they move the business forward and deliver great experiences. Learn more about our Leadership Principles here.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer - Data Modeling & Visualization
description:
Since 2009, Lengow has been the indispensable e\-commerce platform for multi\-channel expansion in the European market: marketplaces, price comparison websites, affiliate marketing, display ad retargeting, social media, etc.


Our Data team


Join a dynamic Tech, Data \& Product team of 50 professionals with diverse expertise. You’ll report to the Head of Data and work closely with our Tech, Product, and business teams.


The Data Team is a key driver of innovation at Lengow. From enabling access to insights for employees to creating custom data products for clients, our mission is to transform raw data into business impact. We’re expanding our scope and shaping the future of data at Lengow.


What the Data team does

* Empower business decisions with relevant insights and accessible data tools.
* Guide product development through data\-driven features, metrics, and insights.
* Manage and optimize custom data products for clients.
* Enhance our data stack and tools for scalability, reliability, and performance.
* Cultivate a data\-first culture by translating business needs into actionable insights.


Your mission


We are seeking a Senior Analytics Engineer — Data Modeling \& Visualization to strengthen the Data Team’s semantic modeling, metrics, and dashboarding capabilities.


With access to vast data — thousands of catalogs, millions of products, and billions of entries scraped from e\-commerce websites — you’ll help transform complex data into reliable models, clear metrics, and useful dashboards for internal and customer\-facing data products.


This role owns the Data Team’s semantic and visualization layer: business\-facing data models, metric definitions, dashboards, validation rules, and documentation. You will work closely with the Product Manager, who owns Product\-side framing, prioritization, stakeholder alignment, and business acceptance. Your role is to translate Product and business needs into reliable models, clear KPIs, useful dashboards, and maintainable data products.


This is a senior technical role at the intersection of analytics engineering, data modeling, and data visualization. It is not a Product Manager role or a pure Data Engineering role. It is also not focused on ad hoc reporting: requests should be turned into reusable, maintainable data assets whenever they create recurring value.


Your key responsibilities:

* Own the semantic and visualization layer of Lengow’s internal and customer\-facing data products.
* Define and document KPIs, dimensions, facts, grains, filters, assumptions, and business rules.
* Design reusable analytical models and semantic layers across dashboards and data products.
* Build and improve dashboards in Looker Studio that are clear, useful, performant, and decision\-oriented.
* Transform Product and business requirements into modeled datasets, dashboard specifications, validation rules, and documentation.
* Write advanced SQL transformations and contribute to dbt workflows.
* Collaborate with Senior Data Engineers on upstream data quality, data contracts, performance, reliability, and maintainability.
* Challenge unclear metric definitions, incomplete acceptance criteria, misleading visualizations, and one\-off requests that should become reusable data products.
* Communicate assumptions, limitations, edge cases, feasibility, risks, and trade\-offs clearly to technical and non\-technical stakeholders.


Recruitment Process* Pre\-interview: Chat with Alexandre, Head of People (30').
* Team interview: Meet Sebastien (VP Data) and team members (60').
* Final interview: Present a technical case to Sebastien and Olivier (Chief Product and Technology Officer) (60').

  

**Requirements**  

We’re looking for a senior data professional who combines technical rigor, strong data modeling skills, visualization expertise, and business understanding.


You should be able to understand a business question, challenge vague definitions, design the right analytical model, and deliver a dashboard or data product that can be trusted over time.


Here’s what you bring to the table:

* Experience: 5\+ years in analytics engineering, data visualization engineering, BI engineering, data engineering, or a similar data role.
* Data modeling: strong understanding of facts, dimensions, grains, aggregations, metric definitions, semantic consistency, and business rules.
* Data visualization: proven ability to design dashboards that are not only visually clear, but useful for real decisions.
* Engineering fluency: advanced SQL, strong analytical rigor, and good understanding of data quality, lineage, testing, and transformation workflows.
* Collaboration: ability to work with Product, business stakeholders, and Senior Data Engineers without becoming a substitute Product Manager or a support desk.
* Mindset: autonomous, structured, constructive, and able to push back when definitions, requirements, or implementation choices are unclear or unsafe.
* Tools \& tech: experience with SQL, BigQuery, Google Cloud Platform, dbt, Airflow, Cube.js, Looker Studio, Power BI, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL. Familiarity with ETL/ELT tools such as Talend or Apache NiFi is a plus in our current context.


We value your ideas and welcome recommendations on tools, modeling practices, visualization standards, and data product quality.


Bonus points if you:

* Know and are passionate about web, e\-commerce, marketplaces, retail, SaaS, or product analytics.
* Have worked on customer\-facing dashboards or data products.
* Have experience with semantic layers, metrics layers, or governed KPI frameworks.
* Have experience with data contracts or data quality frameworks.
* Have strong UX instincts for data products and dashboards.


What success looks like
Success will be evaluated through the quality, reliability, adoption, and maintainability of internal and customer\-facing data products.


Examples of successful outcomes include:

* Critical KPIs have clear definitions, grains, assumptions, and validation rules.
* Dashboards are trusted, documented, actively used, and decision\-oriented.
* Dashboard logic is implemented in reusable modeled datasets instead of duplicated across reports.
* Stakeholders understand metric behavior, limitations, and edge cases.
* Product/Data collaboration with the Product Manager is structured and repeatable.

Technical environment
Our environment includes SQL, BigQuery, Google Cloud Platform, Cube.js, dbt, Airflow, Looker Studio, Power BI, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Talend, Apache NiFi, and internal and customer\-facing analytics use cases.

title: Product Owner - Mainloop
location: Sant Cugat del Vallès, CT, ES
description:
**Product Owner**
=================


Own the product, not the ticket queue — the business relationship, the backlog, acceptance, and whether the thing actually gets used.


Mainloop is a **new engineering team inside an established international group**. We are in Barcelona, we are being built from scratch this year, and we have the backing, the customers and the product portfolio of a company that has been around for decades. You get the interesting part of a new team without the part where you check whether payroll clears.


Two more things about where this comes from and where it goes. **The group has been running a techlab in Casablanca for more than eight years** — Barcelona is its second, built to sit closer to the teams we build for, and AI\-native from the first commit, because it starts from a blank page. And the plan does not stop at internal work: **within about a year and a half we intend to externalise** — external clients, our products sold on the market, products developed for it. The first eighteen months are deliberately spent building as much as possible for the group while the machine gets set up. You would arrive at the start of that curve, not after it.


What we build is the software that automates professional\-services work — across roughly fifteen countries, for businesses drowning in administration: the forms, the approvals, the reconciliations, the spreadsheet somebody rebuilds every month. We work in two halves. One half goes into a business, finds out what really happens there, and proves fast whether an idea is worth having. **The other half — your half — takes what is proven and owns it for years: gathers the needs, keeps building, gets it adopted, and makes sure it stays worth having.** Most automation teams stop at the demo. The entire point of ours is that we do not.

**We are not looking for a backlog administrator.** If your last role was turning other people's decisions into tickets and running the ceremonies around them, this is a different job. Here you are the product manager *and* the product owner: there is no one above you writing the strategy for your products, and no one below you writing the stories. What should exist, in what order, and whether what shipped is right — that is yours.

##### **What the job actually is**


A product arrives with a handover pack — already proven with its stakeholders by the first half of the team, already hardened for production. From day one it belongs to you and one developer, as a pair, for its life.

* **You own the relationship with the business.** Real people, in real offices, whose working day your product either improves or does not. You go and sit with them. Not a ticket queue — trust, built in person, held over years.
* **You gather the needs and you decide.** Your users cannot churn — they are in the building, and they will bring you more requests than any team could build. Most of this job is choosing: what moves the outcome, what waits, and what you decline with a reason the person asking can respect. **Saying no well is the defining skill here**, and you will have a product vision to say it from.
* **You write what should exist, precisely.** In our team, coding agents build most of what ships, steered by your developer. Agents amplify whatever they are given: a sharp specification becomes working software astonishingly fast, and a vague one becomes a thousand lines of confidently wrong code. Your needs, rules, edge cases and acceptance criteria are the most load\-bearing documents in the company. Writing them precisely is the highest\-leverage hour of your week.
* **You accept, or you don't.** When something ships, you are the person who checks the behaviour against what you wrote — with your own hands, in the product, against the criteria you set before the build. "The demo looked right" is not acceptance. You will get seriously good at defining what "done right" means in a way that can actually be checked.
* **You get it adopted, and you measure.** Our products do not have revenue to hide behind. A product that ships and is not used is a failure with good release notes. You own the follow\-up, the onboarding of new users with the business, and the number that says whether the thing is working — time saved, error rate, uptake — and you report that number whether it flatters us or not.
* **You carry a portfolio, not a product.** Every product we own is built on the same scaffold and arrives the same shape, which is what makes it possible for one PO to run several — each with its own developer, each with its own business. Variety is structural here: new products keep arriving from the other half of the team.
* **Your first product is real.** A live platform that a business runs on every day — real users, real history, real stakes. You inherit it from the person who has been carrying it, and part of your first months is taken up with the most useful thing a new PO can do: learning it properly before changing it.

##### **Why this job exists — the honest version**


Here is the thing our industry has just learned, and it is the reason we are hiring you: **AI made building fast, and it did not make building the right thing any more likely.** Surveys now find most companies shipping faster with AI while almost none can point to the return. It has never been easier to run, at speed, in the wrong direction.


In a team like ours the engineers steer agents, and implementation is rarely the bottleneck. **The bottleneck is deciding** — what to build, for whom, in what order, and whether what shipped actually did what the business needed. That is not a job the agents do. It is not really a job most engineers want. It is *this* job, and in an AI\-native team it is a more senior, more consequential job than the same title has ever been — because every decision you write down gets built, quickly, exactly as you wrote it.

**What stays yours, permanently:**

* **Deciding what not to build.** The agents will cheerfully build anything. Somebody has to be the person for whom "no" is a complete sentence with a number attached.
* **The relationship.** Being trusted by a business, reading what they need underneath what they ask for, and telling them a favourite idea is not worth it — there is no model for that.
* **Precision about what should exist.** Turning a messy, human, political need into a specification with exactly one correct interpretation is the hardest writing there is, and it is now the closest thing this industry has to source code.
* **Judgement about what came back.** Acceptance, in a world where software appears fast, is the quality bar. You are it.
* **The outcome.** Whether the business is actually better off. Somebody has to own that number rather than the ship date, and it is you.

##### **You will define how the PO role works here**


You are the first. That is not a gap in the org chart — it is the offer.


How product ownership works in an AI\-native team is a genuinely open question in our industry right now, and the honest answer is that nobody's playbook fits yet. Ours will be written here, over your first year, by you and Edouard together: how needs become specs, how acceptance works when agents build, how adoption gets measured, how many products one pair can carry. The POs we hire after you will be onboarded onto the way you built.


If you have ever read a process document and thought *I could have written this better* — this is the job where you get to.

##### **You will get seriously good at building with AI**


We are an AI\-native team, genuinely — not a team that added a Copilot licence. Everyone gets their own Claude Max subscription and the tooling to use it properly, and that includes you. The product people we admire in this market prototype with AI before they ask anyone to build: a rough working version of an idea, made in an afternoon, shown to a stakeholder — because a prototype communicates intent better than any document, and because it kills bad ideas cheaply. You will learn to do that here if you cannot already, and you will learn what makes a specification one an agent builds correctly the first time. That skill is being repriced upward across our entire industry, and this is one of very few jobs where you would practise it daily on products people depend on.

##### **The Mainloop Barcelona certificate**


Something we are building alongside the team, and we think it is genuinely unusual.


Over your first two to three years here you work through a defined body of knowledge — how we build, how we run products, how a need becomes a spec becomes working, adopted software — and when you can demonstrably run a product our way, you are awarded the **Mainloop Barcelona certificate**. It is yours: it goes on your CV, and we intend to make it mean something in this market. For a product person specifically, it certifies the thing the market is newly desperate for — that you can own products in an AI\-native team, end to end, with proof.

##### **How we build**

**Every product starts from the same scaffold, and it is the same in most of our repos — deliberately.** For you that is the whole point: every product in your portfolio has the same shape, so carrying several does not mean holding several different worlds in your head. It also means the handover pack you inherit from the first half of the team actually tells you how the thing works — because it is built the way everything else is built.


You do not need to arrive knowing our tooling, and this ad deliberately lists no technologies. You need to be technical enough to hold your own in an engineering discussion, and to read what an agent produced closely enough to judge it. The rest — our architecture, our patterns, our method — is what we train you on.

##### **Things worth knowing up front**

* **Barcelona is your base, and you will spend real time with the businesses.** The products serve people across roughly fifteen countries, and the relationship is the job — expect regular travel to sit with your users, on us. It is a fraction of what our deployed engineers do, but it is not zero, and the POs who never leave the office are the ones whose products stop being used.
* **Nobody is on call. Ever.** No rota, no pager. Alerts post to a channel and wait for morning. We protect evenings with engineering, not with people.
* **Nobody counts your hours or your tickets.** What gets looked at is whether your products are used, whether the business is better off, and whether your specs held up. Outcomes, not throughput.
* **We are building the team this year, and you will shape how it works.** That is truest of all for this seat — see above.

##### **If you would be moving to Barcelona for this**

**We do not expect you to absorb the cost of relocating, and we would rather say what we cover than leave you to ask.**

* **We pay to get you here.** Flights, your first month's accommodation while you find somewhere of your own, the visa and paperwork costs, and **an agent to handle the bureaucracy** — the NIE, the TIE appointment, the apostilles — instead of leaving you to meet the Spanish administrative system alone. Spanish lessons if you want them — and in this seat they will pay for themselves.
* **A relocation bonus, paid on arrival rather than dripped out.** It is repayable only if you leave within the first eighteen months, and that condition is the reason we can pay it up front — moving countries costs money at the start, not in year two.

**Three things here are worth more than they look on an offer comparison, particularly against a US one:**

* **Healthcare with no premium, no deductible and no network** — from day one, and not tied to staying in this job.
* **Thirty calendar days of holiday — that is 22 working days — plus fourteen public holidays**, roughly seven weeks in total. That is the statutory floor in Spain, not a benefit we are being generous with.
* **Nobody is on call. Ever.** It has its own line above and we mean it literally.

**If you are coming from the United States**, two things are usually worth more than the headline salary gap and almost nobody has done the arithmetic: **a salary here can sit below the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion**, and **federal student loans on an income\-driven plan are assessed on the income that exclusion has already removed.** We are not your tax advisor and you should get one — but ask in the first conversation and we will walk you through the comparison we ran, including the parts where the number comes out smaller.

##### **What we are looking for**

**One bar sits above everything else, so here it is plainly.** You can own a product end to end — the need, the decision, the specification, the acceptance, the outcome — and you are **technical enough to contribute to an engineering discussion and to judge what an AI agent built.** You do not need to code for a living. You do need to have no fear of the inside of the machine. If you read that and thought *that is the job I want*, keep reading.

**Read the rest as a description of the person you will be here, not a checklist you have to arrive with.** Almost nobody ticks all of it on day one, and we would rather hire the judgement and train the rest.

* **You have owned something real.** A product, a platform, a module — something in production, with users, where the backlog, the priorities and the outcome were genuinely yours. We will ask you to walk us through it, and to justify specific decisions inside it.
* **You are interested in how businesses actually work.** Processes, the mess in them, and why people do the odd things they do. Our products automate administrative work, and the PO who finds that boring will be bored.
* **You write with precision, and you like it.** The spec, the acceptance criteria and the "no, because…" are all documents, all read by people (and agents) who were not in the room. If your writing is where your thinking happens, you will be at home.
* **You can say no to someone senior, with a number.** And keep the relationship.
* **You use AI seriously** — for prototyping, for analysis, for your own writing — and you read what it produces the way you would read a colleague's work: with respect and suspicion.
* **You are comfortable with engineers**, and they with you. Our model is one PO and one developer owning each product together. That pair only works if you feed each other context instead of passing tickets over a wall.
* **English, fluently.** It is our working language — we work across roughly fifteen countries. Spanish is a genuine advantage day to day, and for your first product especially. Catalan is not required.
* **Barcelona**, with travel to your businesses.

**We do not care what you studied, and a Scrum certification is neither required nor an advantage.** We care what you have owned, what happened to it, and whether you can talk us through the decisions in it.

##### **How we hire**


Our process is unusual, so here it is up front. Four rounds, and none of them is a puzzle.

* **Fifteen minutes with Edouard.** A short first conversation — who you are, what you are after, and what this actually is. Enough for both of us to work out whether the next one is worth an hour.
* **A thirty\-minute conversation.** What you have owned, how you work, and how you think about it. We will ask you to walk us through a product you owned, and then to justify one specific prioritisation decision inside it: why that, why then, what you declined to do instead. There is no way to prepare for that and it is not meant to catch you out; it is how we tell ownership from proximity.
* **A conversation with our Casablanca team.** The group has run a tech lab there for more than eight years. You get people who have run production at real scale asking their own questions — and you get to ask them yours, including the ones you would rather not ask the person hiring you.
* **A working session built around a real product.** You read a real handover pack, sit with a real stakeholder, decide what matters, write the specification and the acceptance criteria — and then watch what our agents and your developer counterpart build from it, and tell us whether you would accept it, and what it would be worth. It is the closest thing to the real job we could design, and it works both ways: you will know a great deal about whether you want to work here by the end of it.

Seize ownership and excel with autonomy to enjoy the constant rush of ground\-breaking discovery. Your ability to anticipate sudden shifts and adapt swiftly will prove critical as you make your mark in an environment that rewards initiative and resilience.


**Responsibilities**
--------------------


**Job ID** R\-259586 **Date posted** 09/07/2026
“It is critical that we build and maintain our rich tradition of clinical expertise in support of developing life\-changing medicines for patients.” –Jose Baselga


The Baselga Cancer Research Scholars Program, initiated in 2020, is a 2\-year immersive education and research program for early\-career Oncologists who are inspired by science and by how clinical development has the potential to transform patient care. As part of a competitively selected cohort of Scholars, you will join an accelerated development track within Oncology R\&D. With individualized mentorship, there is opportunity to learn from a diverse group of experts across the drug development continuum, playing a pivotal role in channelling our scientific capabilities to make a positive impact on changing patients’ lives. Selected Scholars will join the current cohort of Baselga Cancer Research Scholars, building a vibrant community of drug developers. We are currently recruiting for the 2027 class with an aim to start the position in summer\-autumn 2027\.


**About AstraZeneca Oncology Research \& Development**


Our Oncology strategy is built with one goal in mind – pushing the boundaries of science to deliver life\-changing medicines to patients. We have a passion for discovery and a broad pipeline of next\-generation medicines, and together with a focus on execution excellence, we aim to expand treatment options and improve outcomes for patients with solid and haematological cancers. We’re pioneering innovative research across six scientific platforms: Tumor drivers and resistance; Immuno\-oncology, DNA damage response, Antibody drug conjugates, Epigenetics and Cell therapies.


Our ambition is to eliminate cancer as a cause of death. It’s our big vision that unites and inspires us. With multiple indications and high\-quality molecules at all stages of our innovative pipeline, we keep pushing forward. Focusing on cutting\-edge science with the latest technology to achieve breakthroughs. AZ is a place built on courage, curiosity and collaboration – we make bold decisions driven by patient outcomes.


**What you’ll do**


The 2027 AZ Baselga Cancer Research Scholars cohort will join AstraZeneca at a time of tremendous growth and acceleration in the oncology biologics portfolio. Working in a fast\-paced and dynamic work environment you will experience increasing levels of responsibility, following a structured learning plan in the following domains:


1\) **Clinical Study Assignment:** You will join a clinical study team and build experience as a medical leader in clinical development which could be in Early Clinical Development, Late Clinical Development, or one year in each. You will participate in weekly clinical and scientific meetings related to your clinical study, complete AstraZeneca training programs and participate in internal and external scientific meetings. You will work in a cross functional environment, contributing to and supporting Department/Clinical initiatives to improve the quality and content of all clinical programs as well as the cross functional/organization processes designed to effectively deliver our R\&D portfolio.


Specific duties and major responsibilities for the longitudinal medical project may include any of the following:


* Serving as medical director with primary responsibility for patient safety and conduct of assigned trials as well as overall data interpretation and safety surveillance
* Establishing and approving scientific methods for design and implementation of applicable clinical protocols, data collection systems, and final reports
* Assisting in design of clinical development plans and overall strategy for compounds, therapeutic classes of compounds or indications in light of developments in the area of clinical and pharmaceutical oncology
* Collaborating with pre\-clinical and translational sciences, and senior management in assessing requirements for emerging products
* Participating in the selection and management activities of CROs
* Supervising project team members in planning, conducting and evaluating clinical trials
* Planning and managing investigator meetings, advisory boards and other scientific committees

2\) **Rotational program:** During the course of your program, you will be involved in 3\-6 month long rotations across various groups to gain a better understanding of the cross\-functional departments. This could include:


* Patient safety
* Clinical operations
* Regulatory affairs
* Biostatistics
* Medical affairs
* Translational medicine or precision medicine

3\) **Longitudinal Research Project:** You will have opportunity to lead an innovative research project of your choosing for the duration of the 2\-year program, which may be an area of special interest to you and AstraZeneca, or alternatively focus on one or more of the rotational functions. You will be able to harness rich internal datasets and expertise, aiming to deliver a research project at the end of the Program which will be presented to key internal stakeholders, at a key scientific meeting and published in a peer\-reviewed journal.

MD or equivalent required; ideally board certified (or eligible) preferred in Oncology or Haematology/Oncology

description:

We help clients grow through AEO and SEO\-driven content strategy, powered by a mix of specialized talent and AI tooling built for the way we work. Our team spans Content Specialists, Growth Leads, Growth Directors, and Editors, all supporting client accounts across multiple pods.


We're looking for an L\&D Coordinator to join Graphite's learning and development team. You'll work directly with our L\&D Manager to keep onboarding, training, and internal learning programs running day to day, then grow into building more of that content yourself as you settle in.


We're not looking for someone to just execute a checklist. This role needs a creative problem\-solver who writes well, thinks ahead, and brings ideas for how to do things better, not just someone who completes tasks as assigned. You'll have ownership over how programs get built and communicated, and we want someone who's enthusiastic and curious about using AI to work smarter, whether that's research, dashboards, or automating the repetitive parts of the job.


This is a foundational role on a growing team. Graphite runs L\&D through as a single person team now, and this hire is what lets it scale. You'll start focused on execution: building onboarding materials, tracking program data, and keeping our internal L\&D channel active.


Within your first year, you'll take on more content creation, community\-building, and program facilitation as you learn the business and our programs.

**This is a remote role, open to candidates based in Madrid only at this time.**

**Who you are**

* A clear, engaging writer who can make training content feel practical \& exciting.
* Organized and proactive by nature, you flag problems before they become blockers.
* Genuinely curious, you like figuring out a better way to do something rather than just doing it the way you've always done it.
* Comfortable using AI tools for research, building lightweight dashboards, or automating repetitive work, and excited to find more ways to do that.
* A creative thinker who brings ideas to the table, not just someone who waits to be told what to do.

**What you'll do**

* Build onboarding materials and online programs for new hires across our Growth, Editorial, and other areas across the company, using established templates and frameworks.
* Track completion data, quiz scores, and skill baselines, and keep our reporting trackers current.
* Coordinate logistics for training sessions and workshops: scheduling, reminders, working session setup, and feedback collection.
* Post regular updates to our L\&D Slack channel: session recaps, upcoming sessions, and useful resources for the team.
* Support our intern and shadowing programs with onboarding, tracking, and kickoff logistics.
* Help maintain compliance training materials, including templates for subject\-matter experts and completion tracking.
* As you grow in the role, take on drafting original training content (modules, decks, videos) and help build out a more consistent L\&D content and community presence company\-wide.

**Required experience**

* 1\-2 years of experience in training coordination, HR, learning operations, or a related role.
* Strong writing skills, with a portfolio or writing sample that shows range.
* Comfortable working in a Learning Management System (we use Disco) or similar platform.
* Hands\-on experience using AI tools for research, reporting, or workflow automation, this isn't just familiarity, we want to see how you've actually used them.
* Excellent organizational skills, with close attention to detail.
* Ability to work independently in a fully remote environment.
* Genuine interest in learning and development as a career path.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with content creation: writing, video, or presentation design.
* Experience with data collection and analysis, including building charts and reports on training data.
* Familiarity with growth marketing, SEO, or AEO concepts (or willingness to learn them quickly, since our training content covers this space).
* Experience running or contributing to an internal community, newsletter, or knowledge\-sharing initiative.
* Spanish language skills (a plus given our team's regional makeup).

**How we’ll help:**


Graphite’s mission is to create an environment where you build the best work of your career. In order to facilitate this, we provide:

* **Process As Needed** \- We view the process as a way to empower better work, not as a series of dogmatic rules. We develop the best internal processes as we do products \- through iteration, measurement, and continuous improvement.
* **Autonomy** \- We trust you to be excellent at what you do. We will provide as much support as needed when needed, but no more. You will have autonomy and agency to drive projects forward, and own decisions and outcomes.
* **Flexible Work Environment** \- Everyone’s optimal work style is unique. We operate as a distributed team across the US, Canada, Latin America, and Europe. We optimize for productivity and performance, not time spent in an office. Help us build an optimal work environment that fits you as an individual.
* **Compensation** \- We want to work with the best people in the World and compensate accordingly.
* **Vacation \& Time Off** \- In order to be the best version of yourself, you need time to recharge. We offer flexible PTO. Take the time when you need it.
* **Benefits** \- We will ensure you have quality healthcare coverage and opportunities to further your education.

title: Head of Digital
description:
**¿Todo listo para tu nueva aventura?**


En blue banana creemos firmemente que las personas son el centro de nuestro desarrollo como marca.


Por ello, nuestro objetivo es atraer el mejor talento para seguir creciendo en este proyecto sin límites, donde trabajamos para empoderar a las nuevas generaciones a hacer de sus vidas una aventura. Nuestra misión nos invita a conectar con nuestro consumidor de una manera significativa, a través de la creación de contenido, de historias inspiradoras y de productos icónicos de alta calidad, responsables con el medioambiente.


No solo somos una marca, ¡SOMOS UN ESTILO DE VIDA! y queremos influir positivamente en el mundo.


¿Te identificas con nuestra pasión y propósito? Si es así, sigue leyendo y descubre cómo puedes ser parte de esta emocionante misión.


**Tu contribución en blue banana brand será excepcional si desarrollas estas funciones:**


Hacer crecer de forma rentable la venta online y de marketplaces, maximizar la eficiencia de la inversión en captación, elevar la recurrencia y el valor de cliente, y garantizar una experiencia de cliente coherente entre online y tienda. Dueño/a de ingresos, margen de contribución, coste de captación, devoluciones y coste de servicio del canal digital, y del roadmap de plataforma, datos y automatización que lo sostiene.

* **Marketplaces:** Apertura, consolidación y rentabilidad de El Corte Inglés, Decathlon, Veepee y Zalando: catálogo, precios, procesos y reconciliación.
* **Internacionalización:** Mercados prioritarios (PT, DE, FR, IT), monedas y pagos locales, localización de contenido y políticas de envío y devolución por mercado; modelización de escenarios de inversión (ROAS objetivo, break\-even).
* **Paid media:** Estrategia y presupuesto en Meta, TikTok y Google; objetivos de MER, blended ROAS y CAC por mercado; decisiones de escalar, pausar o reasignar en base a datos.
* **Medición y atribución** Gobierno de tagging, UTMs y atribución GA4/Shopify; detección y corrección de errores de clasificación de canales.
* **CRM y loyalty (Klaviyo):** Flows de ciclo de vida, calendario de campañas y peso del email en la facturación; modelo RFM y de recurrencia, programa de segunda compra, win\-back e identificación de cliente en tienda para unificar la ficha omnicanal.
